Oxford is a thriving area with strong demand for reliable central heating installation and repair services. Local properties range from period Victorian and Edwardian homes through to modern new-build developments, each presenting different plumbing requirements and challenges.

Our Gas Safe registered engineers serve all areas of Oxford and the surrounding Oxfordshire region. Whether you're in the town centre or the surrounding residential areas, we provide prompt, professional central heating services with transparent pricing and no hidden call-out charges.

With years of experience working across Oxfordshire, our engineers understand the specific plumbing challenges faced by local homeowners. From the older pipe infrastructure common in period properties to the modern systems found in newer developments, our team has the expertise to handle any central heating installation and repair requirement.

We cover all postcodes across Oxford with same-day availability for urgent work. All our engineers are fully qualified, insured, and committed to leaving your property clean and tidy after every job.

faqs.q: How long does a central heating installation take?
faqs.a: A full central heating installation in a 3-bedroom semi-detached property typically takes 3-5 days. Larger properties or complex layouts take longer.

faqs.q: How many radiators do I need?
faqs.a: A qualified heating engineer calculates the heat loss for each room based on size, insulation, window area, and orientation, then sizes radiators accordingly. Undersized radiators are the most common reason homes never get warm enough.

faqs.q: What is a power flush and do I need one?
faqs.a: A power flush forces water and chemicals through your heating system at high velocity to remove sludge and corrosion debris. It's recommended before fitting a new boiler to an old system — debris from old pipes can damage a new boiler within months.

faqs.q: Should I add inhibitor to my heating system?
faqs.a: Yes — inhibitor prevents internal corrosion and sludge buildup, extending the life of your boiler and pump significantly. It should be added to all new installations and refreshed every 2-3 years.

localParagraph: Oxford's diverse housing stock presents a wide range of central heating challenges for homeowners and landlords across the city. From the Victorian terraced streets of Jericho and East Oxford to the post-war semis of Cowley and the newer builds around Barton, each property era brings its own boiler and pipework considerations. The mixed water hardness found throughout Oxfordshire means that limescale accumulation can vary considerably from one postcode to the next, making it worthwhile to have a local engineer assess whether a scale inhibitor or magnetic filter would benefit your system. Hard water deposits are a common cause of boiler inefficiency and reduced radiator performance, so understanding your local supply is genuinely useful when planning maintenance or upgrades. Oxford's blend of period conversions, student lets, and family homes also means that heating systems often require bespoke solutions rather than a one-size-fits-all approach. Engaging a Gas Safe registered engineer familiar with the region's property types and water conditions is the most reliable way to keep your system running efficiently throughout the colder months.
whatItInvolves: Central heating installation or replacement involves fitting a new boiler, radiators, pipework, and controls to heat your home efficiently. A full system installation is a major project typically taking 3-5 days. A system upgrade — replacing radiators and adding smart controls to an existing boiler — takes 1-2 days. Both must be carried out by a Gas Safe registered engineer.
process: Survey: calculate heat loss per room and size radiators accordingly. First fix: run new pipework routes, fit radiator brackets, position boiler location. Second fix: hang radiators, connect boiler, fit programmer and thermostatic radiator valves. Commission: fill system, add inhibitor, balance radiators for even heat distribution, test all controls. Register with Building Control. Full system flush prior to filling removes debris that causes cold spots and pump failure.
whatToExpect: A full central heating installation in a 3-bed semi takes 3-5 days. You'll be without heating and hot water during the works — plan around this in winter. Modern systems with smart thermostats (Nest, Hive, Tado) can reduce heating bills by 20-30% through accurate scheduling. Your installer should provide a full commission certificate and Building Regulations notification.
